I don't have NAS-Bench-201 accuracy data in this session, so these are priors based on how the cell search space typically behaves, not measured interaction effects. Each hypothesis also has to hold on all three datasets by a meaningful margin, so I've kept most estimates low. Claims that edit an edge whose parent condition is about that same edge (0, 21, 27) are the most ambiguous, since "effect" depends on which baseline operation is being replaced.
